items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Recommendation: block security-sensitive releases and public exposure; conditionally allow ordinary reversible growth only when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Evidence: fleet-doctor has no completed run; operations has no deploy, uptime, or error sweep results; security sitefacts are unknown across 61 managed sites; and authentication, secrets, runtime isolation, release integrity, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness are unevidenced. Compliance HTTPS checks support only limited transport evidence, not complete TLS or security assurance. Risk severity: high for go-live, public exposure, and security-sensitive releases; medium for strictly contained reversible growth. Exact decision: retain the private/preview-only gate, continue existing read-only evidence work, and require owner disposition before any security-sensitive implementation proceeds.

Retain the existing readiness-only plan for complicated.work, but do not admit build, deploy, credential, configuration, dependency, or public-exposure work. Re-review only after dated evidence covers access boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release controls, TLS, dependency provenance, data-flow protection, monitoring, incident response, and security.txt or disclosure readiness.
Keep security-sensitive releases and public exposure blocked. The routed rc-9.com change must remain isolated, reversible, dependency-free, credential-free, and configuration-neutral.
